tagline: Misty ridges, historic valleys and waterfall walks across two states
airports: Knoxville (TYS) for the Tennessee side, Asheville (AVL) for North Carolina

bestTime.text: Wildflowers and high waterfalls; synchronous fireflies in late May by lottery.
Every road open and car-free Wednesdays in Cades Cove, but the busiest and haziest months.
Fall color from the ridges down. Kuwohi Road and Roaring Fork close Nov. 29.
Quiet trails and snow up high; several roads closed and Newfound Gap Road can close for ice.

tips: Buy a parking tag before you drive in. Stops over 15 minutes need one.
Check the NPS closures page the day before. Laurel Falls Trail is closed until 2027.
There is no gas or restaurant inside the park. Carry water and snacks.
Stay well back from bears and at least 25 yards from elk.
Download maps and this itinerary. Cell service drops out across much of the park.

itineraries.title: Three days in the Smokies
itineraries.summary: The ridge road and the high point on day one, waterfalls and the old Elkmont community on day two, and Cades Cove before you leave. Laurel Falls is left out because it is closed until 2027.
itineraries.season: Built for April to Nov. 29, when Kuwohi Road and Roaring Fork are open. Each stop on those roads has a winter swap.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.subtitle: Orientation, the state line and a high-point sunset

stops.text: Check in, then buy a parking tag in town or at Sugarlands before you head into the park.
Pick up a map, read the closures board and walk the short paved nature trail behind the visitor center.
Drive Newfound Gap Road up to the Tennessee and North Carolina line for the Rockefeller Memorial and long ridge views.
stops.status: Open year-round, closes for snow and ice

stops.text: Walk the short, steep paved path to the Kuwohi tower on the park's highest point. The lot fills near sunset.
stops.swap: From Nov. 30 to spring, watch the light from the Newfound Gap overlook instead.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.subtitle: Roaring Fork, Grotto Falls and the Elkmont cabins

stops.text: Drive the narrow one-way loop past homesteads, streams and the Place of a Thousand Drips.
stops.status: Open Apr 17 to Nov 29 (2026). No buses, trailers or motor homes.
stops.swap: In winter, walk the Gatlinburg Trail from Sugarlands along the river. It is one of two park trails that allow dogs.

stops.text: Hike the Trillium Gap Trail from Roaring Fork to walk behind Grotto Falls. Bear cautions have been posted on this trail.
stops.status: Reached only while Roaring Fork is open
stops.swap: In winter, or while Laurel Falls stays closed, walk Little River Trail from Elkmont toward Huskey Branch Falls.

stops.text: Wander the restored cabins of the old Elkmont resort community and follow the Little River upstream.
stops.status: Open. Access is limited during the late-May firefly event.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.theme: Cades Cove and a mountain finale
plan.subtitle: Wildlife, the Cable Mill and the Foothills Parkway

stops.text: Drive the one-way loop early, when fog sits in the fields and deer, turkeys and bears are most often seen. Stay in your car at bear jams.
stops.status: Open year-round. Car-free on Wednesdays May 6 to Sept 30 (2026).

stops.text: Stop midway at the Cable Mill and the visitor center for the historic buildings and restrooms.
Leave by the Foothills Parkway for open ridge views from Look Rock on your way out through Townsend.

itineraries.title: One day in the Smokies: across the ridge
itineraries.summary: A first visit that climbs Newfound Gap Road to the state line, with a river walk that replaces the closed Laurel Falls.
itineraries.season: Built for April to Nov. 29, when Kuwohi Road and Roaring Fork are open. Winter swaps are given at each stop that closes.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.theme: Sugarlands to the state line and back
plan.subtitle: The ridge road, the high point and the old Elkmont community

stops.text: Buy your parking tag if you do not have one, check the closures board, and walk the short nature trail.
Drive up to the state line overlook. Expect it to be colder and windier than town.
stops.status: Open year-round, closes for snow and ice

stops.text: Take Kuwohi Road out to the park's highest point and walk up to the tower.
stops.swap: From Nov. 30 to spring the road is closed. Drive down to Elkmont and walk Little River Trail instead.

stops.text: Walk past the restored Elkmont cabins and follow Little River Trail upstream, a walk the park suggests while Laurel Falls is closed.
Loop the one-way Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail and come out at the edge of Gatlinburg.
stops.status: Open Apr 17 to Nov 29 (2026). No buses, trailers or motor homes.
stops.swap: In winter, walk the Gatlinburg Trail from Sugarlands instead.

itineraries.title: Two days on the quiet side
itineraries.summary: Two slower days from Townsend: Cades Cove at first light, Tremont and the Foothills Parkway, then a history walk at Elkmont.
itineraries.season: Works all year. Abrams Falls Trail was closed through Sept. 30, 2026, so confirm it has reopened before adding it.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.subtitle: Wildlife, the Cable Mill, Tremont and a ridge sunset

stops.text: Start the one-way loop as early as you can. Use pullouts only and stay in your car around bear jams.
stops.status: Open year-round. Car-free on Wednesdays May 6 to Sept 30 (2026).

stops.text: Stop midway at the Cable Mill and visitor center.
Turn up Tremont Road for a quiet streamside walk toward the Lynn Camp Prong cascades.
Drive the Foothills Parkway and walk up to the Look Rock tower before sunset.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.subtitle: A history walk and the main visitor center

stops.text: Walk the restored cabins of the Elkmont historic district, then follow Little River Trail toward Huskey Branch Falls.
stops.status: Open. Access is limited during the late-May firefly event.

stops.text: Continue along Little River Road to Sugarlands for the exhibits and film, and pick up a Junior Ranger book if you have children.
